title: Sand Dunes: They Are What You Think They Are
summary: Josh and Chuck explain how sand dunes form and move, covering the three ways wind transports sand (saltation, creep, suspension), the angle of repose, and the main dune types: crescentic (barchan), transverse, linear, star, parabolic/blowout, composite, lithified dunes, and subaqueous dunes. They discuss coastal dune ecology (pioneer grasses, nutrients from seaweed, pine forest climax), how dunes protect shorelines and why hurricane-damaged dunes take decades to recover, dune fauna, and threats such as deforestation and off-road vehicles. The episode ends with tour announcements and a listener mail story about Chuck's advice on speeding tickets.

segments.title: Tour announcement and opening banter
segments.summary: Tour dates for Chicago and Toronto are announced. Josh and Chuck banter about sand dunes, desert dunes versus coastal dunes, and a dune in Japan.

segments.title: How sand dunes form and move
segments.summary: Dunes need loose sand, wind, and an obstacle. Sand moves by saltation, creep, and suspension. Dunes migrate while keeping their shape, depending on wind regime.

segments.title: Dune growth, crest collapse and angle of repose
segments.summary: As sand piles on the slip face, a crest forms and can collapse in an avalanche. The stable slope is the angle of repose, about 30 to 34 degrees. Wind strength and direction shape dune height and spread.

segments.title: Dune types and confusion over terminology
segments.summary: Hosts introduce dune classification and note that sources disagree on names. Crescentic dunes are the most common on Earth and Mars, and they can move quickly and merge with each other.

segments.title: Transverse, linear, star, parabolic and composite dunes
segments.summary: Transverse dunes are perpendicular to the wind. Linear dunes are long ridges shaped by seasonal shifting winds. Star dunes build upward from multidirectional winds and can be very tall. Parabolic dunes are anchored at the arms by vegetation or moisture. Composite dunes are large combinations, such as draas.

segments.title: Lithified dunes and subaqueous dunes
segments.summary: Lithified dunes are hardened ancient dunes, such as slick rock, with mineral layers from water. Subaqueous dunes form underwater in rivers and canals and can increase flood risk by increasing flow resistance.

segments.title: Coastal dunes, plants and recovery
segments.summary: Coastal dunes form from waves bringing sand ashore. Rotting seaweed supplies nutrients for pioneer grasses whose roots bind the sand. Shrubs and heaths follow, and the dune ecosystem can eventually become a pine forest. Dunes protect shorelines, and after hurricanes like Sandy they can take decades to recover.

segments.title: Dune wildlife, threats, and singing dunes
segments.summary: Drought-tolerant plants, rodents, snakes, lizards, insects, and birds live on dunes. Dung beetles are found on every continent except Antarctica. Threats include deforestation, trampling, and off-road vehicles. Singing dunes are mentioned as dry sand avalanching.

segments.title: Listener mail: speeding ticket advice
segments.summary: Camber Solberger, a grad student, writes that she followed Chuck's advice on surrendering to the law after speeding and avoided a ticket and insurance increase.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts invite listener contact through the website and email and close the episode.
